channel.title: Israel National News Flashes
channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: Bomb threat forces Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv to Vienna to divert to Sofia
item.description: Austrian Airlines flight from Ben Gurion Airport to Vienna declares an in-flight emergency following a reported bomb threat. No explosive device has been confirmed.

item.title: Ron Dermer among eight honored for contributions to Israel
item.description: Prestigious award presented on Yom Ha'aliyah recognizes English-speaking immigrants whose contributions have made a lasting impact on the State of Israel

item.title: Axios: Trump breaks precedent with dramatic Netanyahu endorsement ahead of Israel elections
item.description: Nine days before Israel’s elections, Trump gives Netanyahu his “Complete and Total Endorsement" in an unprecedented intervention, Axios’ Barak Ravid reports.

item.title: Minister harassed at hospital days after birth of son
item.description: Negev and Galilee Minister Yitzhak Waserlauf is verbally harassed by left-wing activist while visiting Tel Aviv clinic with newborn son.

item.title: Rabbi Yitzhak Yosef: Jewish law forbids voting for Ben Gvir's party
item.description: Rabbi Yitzhak Yosef rules that supporting Otzma Yehudit is prohibited under Jewish law because of Itamar Ben Gvir's visits to the Temple Mount and his encouragement of others to ascend the site.

item.title: Ofir Deli, 43, from Eli, was killed in a motorcycle accident in Thailand
item.description: An Israeli was killed in a motorcycle accident in Thailand’s Krabi province. His family has been notified, and the Foreign Ministry is arranging the return of his body to Israel. The accident is under investigation.

item.description: What is your ark?‫‬

item.title: How Obama’s warped, insidious narrative distorts historical fact
item.description: In Belfast, Obama repeated a dishonest, mendacious, and vile charge while concealing the evidence needed to judge it - because that evidence would refute it. Opinion.

item.title: IDF cancels leave on Election Day amid fears of Iranian attack
item.description: IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir orders troops to remain on duty during Israel's October 27 elections amid fears of a regional escalation involving Iran or its proxies.

item.title: Shas MK warns: Every wasted vote hands power to the left
item.description: Former minister Michael Malkieli warns haredi voters who stay home or support parties unlikely to enter Knesset could help bring left to power, threaten Israel's Jewish identity.

item.title: Benjamin Netanyahu: 'We are heading for a great victory; it's not far off'
item.description: Netanyahu rejects claims he was part of the pre-October 7th 'conception,' defends his 'total victory' pledge, and vows to establish a balanced commission of inquiry if reelected.

item.title: Trump throws support behind Netanyahu ahead of elections
item.description: US President Donald Trump announces support for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, calling him a 'great warrior' and 'even greater partner for peace.'

item.title: Rabbi Smotrich has a special routine on election day
item.description: Rabbi Chaim Yerucham Smotrich explains why he wears a suit when going to vote and warns that a minority government would undermine the Jewish majority.

item.title: New Iranian FM: 'I’ve been on the hit list for 35 years. Trump will be picking up bodies'
item.description: Iran’s new defense minister claims he has been on a hit list for 35 years. After his predecessor was killed, he threatened Israel and the US and revealed how Iran fortifies its military facilities.

item.title: Following Paris synagogue vandalism, Minister Sofer orders acceleration of French aliyah
item.description: Following Paris synagogue vandalism, Minister Sofer orders acceleration of French aliyah

item.title: Former soccer player Eyal Berkovich: 'I was scared they would poison me'
item.description: Eyal Berkovic recalls tensions with Muslim teammates at Manchester City: '12 Muslims against Eyal,' also describing his suspicions about the team’s chef, 'I was scared they would poison me.'

item.title: Aliyah in the spirit of Na’aseh v’Nishma
item.description: Aliyah is a tikun for The Sin of the Spies.

item.title: Iran’s new defense minister: Heavy fighter jet built domestically expected to take flight next year
item.description:
Iran’s new Defense Minister, Mehrdad Ahlaghki Ketabchi, announced that Iran is making progress in developing an indigenously produced heavy fighter jet, expressing hope that the aircraft will make its maiden flight in 2027.
According to the minister, the aircraft’s initial testing phases are scheduled to take place later this year. The announcement comes as Iran pursues plans to develop independent capabilities to manufacture heavy, multirole fighter jets.

item.title: Stolen car driver tries to ram police vehicle near Tekoa, arrested after officers shoot at tires
item.description:
A police chase involving a vehicle stolen from Jerusalem ended with the arrest of a suspect near Tekoa after he reportedly endangered officers and attempted to ram a police vehicle. During the pursuit, officers fired at the vehicle’s tires in an attempt to stop it.
After the vehicle came to a halt, the suspect attempted to flee on foot toward nearby orchards. Officers continued pursuing him and managed to apprehend him.

item.title: Trump on riots in France: ‘Immigration of people with hatred in their hearts destroyed the country'
item.description:
President Donald Trump commented on the riots that took place in France yesterday.
Trump wrote on Truth Social: “France is burning! The immigration of people from a completely different world, people whose hearts are filled with hatred, has destroyed what was once a great and glorious country. Close your borders and take control, before it’s too late!"

item.title: Fearing voter apathy: Leading Torah sages convene emergency meeting
item.description: Amid concerns over haredi voter apathy ahead of the elections, leading Torah sages convened in Bnei Brak, urging voter turnout, political unity, and opposition to yeshiva students’ conscription.

item.title: Israel’s neighborhood Is getting rougher
item.description: What Yemen should teach the West about Israel’s enemies. Opinion.

item.title: New kind of terrorism: 20+ livestock poisoning incidents in Judea and Samaria in one year
item.description: Meir Bertler of Shomer Yosh calls poisoning incidents in Judea and Samaria 'a new form of terrorism,' saying poison is being spread in grazing areas and water sources.

item.title: Hamas flag & stolen license plates: Vehicle inspection leads to weapons discovery in Dura
item.description: An inspection of a suspicious vehicle in Dura uncovered a Hamas flag and stolen Israeli license plates, leading to a search of a nearby garage where handguns and an improvised firearm were discovered.

item.title: Severe scandal at Kaplan Hospital: Blood samples allegedly taken without consent
item.description: Kaplan Medical Center's cardiology chief faces allegations of collecting blood samples without patient consent, weeks after a residency training scandal emerged.

item.title: Are we a wise and discerning people?
item.description: Today, there are wise and discerning haredim are willing to say out loud: "We want to join our brothers and sisters in defending and contributing to our state! Give us ways to do so that respect our principles, and we will be there, with you and for you." Opinion.

item.title: Journalist's response sparks demand for investigation
item.description: Director General of the Ministry of Religious Services demands an investigation into Haaretz journalist Yael Friedson on suspicion of incitement to violence.

item.title: The directive was issued, but the enthusiasm has disappeared
item.description: After days of speculation, the Gerrer Rebbe has instructed his followers to vote for United Torah Judaism. However, the limited wording of his directive and the absence of instructions to campaign have sparked controversy in the political arena.

item.title: Security coordinators descend on IDF HQ over colleague's arrest: ‘A red line was crossed’
item.description: Security coordinators protested outside IDF headquarters in Tel Aviv, demanding intervention over the alleged harsh detention of a colleague from Samaria.
